entry.title: Hours of Service of Drivers: Association of American Railroads and American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association; Application for Exemption Renewal
entry.content: FMCSA announces its final decision to renew and modify the exemption granted to the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association and member railroads (the Associations) from the hours-of-service (HOS) prohibitions against driving after the 14th hour after coming on duty (the 14-hour rule) and against driving after accumulating 60 hours of on duty time within 7 consecutive days, or 70 hours of on duty time within 8 consecutive days (the 60-hour/70-hour rule). The exemption will enable covered drivers to respond to unplanned events that occur outside of, or extend beyond, their normal work hours. FMCSA modifies the previous exemption to limit the categories of unplanned events during which the exemption may be used and to add reporting requirements. In addition, only drivers operating for motor carriers listed in the Appendix to this decision may operate under the exemption. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and has determined that the exemption renewal, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.

entry.title: US Department of Labor secures court order requiring New Jersey employer to pay $700K in back wages, damages to 48 workers denied overtime pay
entry.content: VOORHEES, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment and final order in federal district court requiring a New Jersey drywall installer to pay $725,000 in back wages, damages, and civil money penalties after denying 48 workers overtime pay.The department’s Wage and Hour Division found that P & B Partitions Inc. failed to pay their employees for pre-shift work while they waited for transportation to their jobsites. The failure to pay constitutes a violation under the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime provisions. “Tasks completed to prepare for the job, and in this case, while waiting to get to the worksite, is work that must be compensated,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Charlene Rachor in Southern New Jersey. “Failing to pay workers overtime wages deprives them of their rights, and we will hold employers accountable for such actions.”The consent judgment requires P & B Partitions Inc. to pay $350,000 in back wages, an equal amount in liquidated damages to 48 workers, and requires payment of an additional $25,000 in civil penalties. The judgment was entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey on June 26, 2026.“The U.S. Department of Labor will pursue legal action to ensure that all employees receive the compensation they are legally owed,” said Regional Solicitor of Labor Jeffrey S. Rogoff in New York. “This case demonstrates that employers can face costly consequences if they do not comply with federal wage law.”Employees and employers can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including how workers can use a search tool if they believe they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free WorkWise Timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago Grants to promote mine safety, health education
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago grant funding to two organizations to support education and training initiatives that will help identify and prevent unsafe working conditions in and around the nation’s mines.Administered by the department’s Mine Safety and Health Administration, the Brookwood-Sago Mine Safety grant program helps recipients create training materials, conduct mine safety training, and educational programs designed to protect the safety and health of miners. In awarding the grants, MSHA focused on innovative plans for mine safety and pilot programs that may be useful for miners working in a broad range of positions. The grants also put an emphasis on programs and materials targeting workers in smaller mines that train mine operators and miners about MSHA standards, and emergency response training.Established under the Mine Improvement and New Emergency Response Act of 2006, the grant program honors the miners lost at the Jim Walter Resources #5 mine in Brookwood, Alabama, on Sept. 23, 2001, and at the Sago Mine in Buckhannon, West Virginia, on Jan. 2, 2006.The recipients of the 2026 Brookwood-Sago grants are as follows:RecipientCityState/TerritoryAmountSaelua Medical Corporation Pago PagoAmerican Samoa$170,000University of ArizonaTucsonAZ$80,000

entry.title: US Department of Labor obtains consent order against retirement plan fiduciaries of defunct Chicago law firm for failing to distribute $6.4M in assets
entry.content: CHICAGO – Following a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Labor, a defunct Chicago law firm’s retirement plan distributed $6,498,858 in retirement plan assets to 40 employees. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan. The plan transferred account balances belonging to plan participants it could not locate to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation’s Missing Participants Program.Employers can get help complying with the law through EBSA’s correction programs, which includes the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program. The VFCP allows plan officials to correct violations and avoid excise taxes for prohibited transactions. Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

entry.title: Seal Cove Auto Museum v. John J. Sanford et al.
entry.content:

Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, CONNORS, DOUGLAS, and LIPEZ, JJ.
SEAL COVE AUTO MUSEUM
v.
JOHN J. SANFORD et al.
LIPEZ, J. [¶1] In 2020, the parties to this appeal, Seal Cove Auto Museum , the Richard C. Paine, Jr., Automobile Collection Charitable Trust (the Trust or the Charitable Trust), and the Trust’s trustees, John J. Sanford and John Peabody Monks Higgins (the Trustees) , entered into a settlement agreement and an amended relationship agreement to resolve a legal dispute. In 2022, after the Trust announced a plan to donate $1,000,000 to the Owls Head Transportation Museum, Seal Cove filed a motion to enforce, arguing that the donation to Owls Head violated the Trust’s and the Trustees’ obligations under the agreements. After a bench trial, t he Business and Consumer Docket ( Duddy, J.) denied the motion, and Seal Cove now appeals, primarily asserting that the trial court misinterpreted relevant provisions of the amended relationship agreement and
2 erred in finding that the Trust had not breached that agreement. Upon review of Seal Cove’s arguments, we conclude that they lack merit, and we accordingly affirm. I. BACKGROUND [¶2] This is not the first time that we have addressed an appeal involving these parties. As we explained in Attorney General v. Sanford: Richard Paine Jr. established Seal Cove in 1963 and the Richard C. Paine, Jr., Automobile Collection Charitable Trust (the Trust) in 1986. The Trust and Seal Cove were established to maintain and display Paine ’s large collection of antique automobiles. Following Paine's death in 2007, the Trust acquired most of Paine ’s automobiles and an endowment to support maintenance and display of the automobile collection. entry.title: Standing Order: Standing Order Requiring Paper Filing for Election Day 2026 Emergency Matters
entry.content:
STATE OF MAINE SUPERIOR COURT DISTRICT COURT
STANDING ORDER REQUIRING PAPER FILING FOR ELECTION DAY 2026 EMERGENCY MATTERS
The Maine Judicial Branch (MJB) is implementing the Maine eCourts system – including eFiling – statewide.1 EFileMaine is a practical and efficient document submission system already in use in many courts throughout the state. However, because filings related to Election Day may be uniquely time- sensitive, to ensure timely processing, the MJB will require paper filing under the limited circumstances described below.
It is therefore ORDERED that any emergency Title 21-A filings related to Election Day 2026 filed between 4:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, and 9:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, must be by paper, unless otherwise ordered.2
It is further ORDERED that the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems are SUSPENDED to the extent necessary to give effect to this order.
Dated: 10/28/2026 _____/s/______________________ Chief Justice Robert E. Mullen
Dated: 10/28/2026 ___/s/_______________________ Chief Judge Brent Davis
1 Further information about the Maine eCourts system is available at https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html 2 Any Election Day 2026 filings filed by eFile during this period may not be processed until the next business day after the election.

Judicial Branch Announces Procedure for Emergency Case Filings Regarding Elections

Date: 10/29/2026

AUGUSTA, Maine. The Maine Judicial Branch announced the procedure for emergency case filings regarding elections to be held on November 3, 2026.

Procedure for Election Filings

In order to expedite the review of filings, Superior Court Chief Justice Robert Mullen and District Court Chief Judge Brent Davis issued a standing order on October 28th requiring all filings pertaining to the November 3 election and filed between Friday, October 30, 2026, at 4:00 pm and Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 9:00 pm to be filed on paper at the clerk's office. Filers should NOT use the eFile Maine system for these emergency filings.

Filings submitted on paper will be reviewed immediately by a clerk and can be directed to the appropriate justice for timely review. Filers are also encouraged to put their cell phone numbers or emergency telephone numbers (where they can be reached after hours) on their filings.

State Courts Open Late on November 3

The state courthouses in Bangor, Augusta and Portland will be open until 9:00 p.m. for the purpose of accepting and acting on emergency paper filings regarding elections. A judge, a clerk and a marshal will be on duty at each courthouse.

Availability of Documents to the Media

All public documents related to election filings will be posted on the high-profile page of the Judicial Branchs public website as soon as is practicable.

Androscoggin County Courthouse to Undergo Remediation Efforts

Date: 11/16/2026

Environmental testing conducted after concerns were raised about the condition of the Androscoggin County Courthouse has revealed elevated levels of mold in some areas of the building. The Judicial Branch ceased operations in all affected areas of the building. The Judicial Branch is working with Androscoggin County, who owns the building, to remove the mold and make needed repairs. The building will be retested to make sure that the problems are eradicated before reopening any parts of the building with elevated mold levels.

Judicial Branch Ends Attorney Entry Screening Bypass Program and Announces Procedure for Reimbursement

Date: 11/17/2026

Beginning January 1, 2027, attorneys entering state courthouses will no longer be able to bypass security screening. Attorneys who show their bar cards (which can be downloaded from the Board of Bar Overseers website) will be able to go to the head of the screening line. In some courthouses, there may be a separate "attorneys only" line if resources allow.

Chief Justice Stanfill spoke to the policy change: The Judicial Branch continuously reviews our security protocols to ensure appropriate measures are in place. We believe this policy change provides greater protection for all people using the courthouse. The policy change follows best practices for courthouse security and aligns with the policy of the federal courts in Maine and the state courts of most other New England states.

The Judicial Branch stopped issuing security cards to attorneys in May 2026. Attorneys whose security cards have not expired by January 1, 2027, will be able to receive a pro rata refund of the fee for the unexpired portion. Instructions and the form for requesting a refund are posted on the For Attorneys page of the Judicial Branch website and can be downloaded directly here: https://www.courts.maine.gov/attorneys/atty-security-card-reimbursement.pdf

entry.title: Policy Statement on Jurisdiction and Preemption Under the ICC Termination Act
entry.content: The Surface Transportation Board (STB or Board) is issuing this policy statement on the scope of its jurisdiction over transportation by rail carriers and on preemption of conflicting state and federal laws under the ICC Termination Act of 1995 (ICCTA). The policy statement provides an overview of the Board's jurisdiction and preemption through a review of existing legal precedent, discussing many commonly occurring questions. The Board intends the policy statement to serve as a useful tool for the public to review, in one place, concise explanations from the Board about its jurisdiction and application of preemption, which the Board anticipates will reduce confusion and facilitate the efficient resolution of disputes.

entry.title: Draft 2026 Marine Mammal Stock Assessment Reports
entry.content: NMFS reviewed the Alaska, Atlantic, and Pacific regional marine mammal stock assessment reports (SARs) in accordance with the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA). SARs for marine mammals in all three regions were revised to include new information. NMFS is soliciting public comments on the draft 2026 SARs. We will consider all comments that are received by the close of the comment period.

entry.title: Federal Financial Participation in State Assistance Expenditures; Federal Matching Shares for Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Aid to Needy Aged, Blind, or Disabled Persons for October 1, 2027, Through September 30, 2028
entry.content: The Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (FMAP) and Enhanced Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (eFMAP) for fiscal year 2028 have been calculated pursuant to the Social Security Act (the Act). These percentages will be effective from October 1, 2027, through September 30, 2028. This notice announces the calculated FMAP rates, in accordance with the Act, that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will use in determining the amount of Federal matching for State medical assistance (Medicaid), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Contingency Funds, Child Support collections, Child Care Mandatory and Matching Funds of the Child Care and Development Fund, Title IV-E Foster Care Maintenance payments, Adoption Assistance payments and Kinship Guardianship Assistance payments, and the eFMAP rates for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) expenditures. Table 1 gives figures for each of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. This notice reminds states of adjustments available for states meeting requirements for disproportionate employer pension or insurance fund contributions and adjustments for disaster recovery. At this time, no state qualifies for such adjustments, and territories are not eligible.

entry.title: US Department of Labor applauds federal appeals court decision on administrative exhaustion requirement under federal benefits law
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor applauded a federal appeals court decision allowing employees to bring legal claims directly to federal court if they reasonably suspect fiduciary violations in their employee benefit plans covered under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act.Issued Oct. 13 by the en banc 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, the unanimous decision in Bolton v. Inland Fresh Seafood overturns precedent that required employees to exhaust all administrative remedies under their ERISA-covered employee benefit plans before they could go to federal court. “This decision vindicates the department’s reinvigorated amicus program and its focus on statutory text,” said Solicitor of Labor Jonathan Berry. “ERISA neither explicitly nor implicitly requires hard-working Americans to go anywhere but federal court to vindicate their statutory rights under it. By overruling its precedent that erroneously held otherwise, the 11th Circuit joins all but one of its sister circuits and reinforces ERISA’s uniform statutory framework.”The court held that the exhaustion requirement was not based on ERISA’s text, saying it was an “atextual product of judicial creation based solely on policy reasons.” The court’s opinion also quoted the department’s oral argument, saying “plaintiffs or employers should not be able to contract away or force their employees to contract away their rights under ERISA.” “The decision by the 11th Circuit rightly rejects a judicially invented exhaustion requirement that has no basis in ERISA’s text or Congressional intent,” said Assistant Secretary of Labor for the Employee Benefits Security Administration Daniel Aronowitz. “By aligning with the law’s clear text and Congress's intent to provide participants and beneficiaries direct access to federal court, the court’s decision makes certain that ERISA’s protections are applied as written in the statute itself.”Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

entry.title: US Department of Labor proposes to modernize permanent labor certification recruitment, strengthening protections for American workers
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today issued a proposed rule that would enhance American worker protections when employers apply for certification to hire foreign workers permanently in the United States. The proposed rule modernizes the Permanent Labor Certification program by strengthening recruitment standards and recordkeeping requirements, eliminating administrative exemptions to the statutory labor market test, and improving safeguards for all American workers, especially those affected by layoffs. This proposed update to the PERM program – the first comprehensive set of regulatory reforms to the program in nearly 20 years – will ensure that highly qualified American workers receive fair consideration and first access to job opportunities.“American Workers are the best in the world, and they deserve the first and best job opportunities. Existing regulations have instead allowed companies to sponsor foreign workers without fully considering American workers first,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “This proposed rule change will ensure American workers are first in line for high-skilled, high-paying job opportunities over foreign labor.”The proposed rule would require employers to level the playing field when recruiting workers by using the same channels and methods when advertising jobs. Proposed changes include a requirement to replace print-based job advertisements with online recruiting through employer websites, online job boards, social media, job fairs, and campus recruitment. Employers would also be required to advertise positions for at least 90 calendar days and demonstrate that they made good-faith efforts to recruit qualified American workers. Under the proposal, employers would be prohibited from tailoring job opportunities to foreign workers. The department also proposed to eliminate the administrative exemption employers used to bypass the statutory labor market test for certain occupations. Under the proposal, employers recruiting for physical therapists, nurses, and workers with exceptional abilities in the sciences or arts would be required to consider qualified U.S. workers. The proposed rule also protects qualified American workers affected by layoffs by requiring ongoing consideration of laid off workers throughout the labor certification and immigrant petition processes, and prohibiting certain employers that have laid off American workers within the last 2 years from seeking permanent labor certification for the same or similar positions. Comments on the proposed rule are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. Additional information is available on ETA’s Office of Foreign Labor Certification website.

entry.title: US Department of Labor proposes new class exemption for qualified professional asset managers to protect retirement plans from disruptions
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Employee Benefits Security Administration today proposed a class exemption that would streamline the process for qualified professional asset managers to continue engaging in transactions permitted under Prohibited Transaction Class Exemption 84-14 – also known as the QPAM exemption – following an ineligibility event. The proposed QPAM Re-eligibility Options After Disqualification Class Exemption, known as QROAD, contains safeguards to protect plans and participants through clear, well-established conditions, including the requirement that asset managers seeking relief under the proposed exemption have an independent fiduciary certify their eligibility and compliance.“For years, QPAMs seeking to rely on the beneficial QPAM class exemption following an ineligibility event have had to go through an individual exemption process that can be costly, burdensome, and time-consuming for everyone involved,” said U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “The QROAD class exemption addresses that problem by creating an alternative path to relief while maintaining the high standards of integrity needed to protect affected plans and participants.”Since 1984, the QPAM exemption has provided broad relief for employee benefit plan and IRA transactions that otherwise would be prohibited under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act if the transactions involved a qualified professional asset manager. QPAMs are expected to maintain a high standard of integrity. If the QPAM or certain of its related parties engage in ineligibility events, such as a criminal conviction or prohibited misconduct, it cannot rely on the QPAM exemption for 10 years. The department has granted several individual exemptions over the years that allow QPAMs to continue to rely on the QPAM exemption notwithstanding such disqualification. For such exemptions, QPAMs must demonstrate that their continued reliance on the QPAM exemption would protect and benefit plans and their participants and beneficiaries. Without this exemptive relief, plans could be forced to unwind investments or replace their asset managers. These costly disruptions can reduce plan assets and participants’ retirement savings. Comments on the proposed class exemption are due 60 days from its publication in the Federal Register. Read the proposed QROAD class exemption and fact sheet to learn more.

entry.title: US Department of Labor proposes to update fiduciary rule to affirm Employee Retirement Income Security Act’s exclusive purpose rule
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Employee Benefits Security Administration today issued proposed amendments to the investment duties regulation to clarify the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act.The proposed rule seeks to end the 32-year uncertainty surrounding whether ERISA allows fiduciaries to consider non-financial factors in retirement plan investments, including environmental, social, and governance, and diversity, equity, and inclusion. The proposal gives fiduciaries an affirmative expression of their duty of loyalty, which would clarify that ERISA requires plan fiduciaries to act solely in the interest of the plan’s participants and beneficiaries, and for the exclusive purpose of providing for the interests of participants and beneficiaries in their retirement income or financial benefits under the plan.“President Trump’s Department of Labor is not putting its thumb on the scale for or against any particular investment or asset class,” said U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Our proposed rule makes clear that retirement plan fiduciaries must make investment decisions solely in the financial interests of workers and retirees, not to advance political or social agendas. Our focus is on protecting and growing Americans’ retirement savings, which have reached record levels thanks to President Trump.”If finalized, the proposal would also place a heightened focus on shareholder engagement and proxy voting by fiduciaries to secure the retirement interests of American workers and would avoid the improper pressures and influence placed on plan fiduciaries. This includes voting shares and otherwise attempting to influence corporate behavior through shareholder engagement activities for ESG/DEI purposes. The proposed rule follows the directive in President Trump’s executive order, “Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors,” which instructed the department to strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA.“President Trump has directed the department to assess whether certain proxy advisor firms spreading ESG and DEI are acting solely in the financial interest of plan participants,” said Assistant Secretary for the Employee Benefits Security Administration Daniel Aronowitz. “Our proposed rule does just that by making clear what is, and what isn’t, loyal behavior when it comes to proxy voting and shareholder engagement.” The proposal would remove two departmental inventions that are not consistent with ERISA and may be misused by fiduciaries with ulterior motives – the tiebreaker test and the participant preference provision. Under the tiebreaker test, a fiduciary can say that two investments are “equal” and then pick their preferred investment, which may include ESG funds. Similarly, fiduciaries can elicit the views of participants who support ESG investments and use that as a pretext to permit investments they otherwise would not be allowed to include under federal retirement laws. The proposed rule will be published in the Nov. 24 edition of the Federal Register, with public comments due 60 days after its publication.EBSA ensures the security of retirement, health, and other job-based benefits for American workers and their families. The agency is responsible for protecting more than 155 million workers, retirees, and their families, who are covered by approximately 2.8 million health plans, 837,000 private retirement plans, and 521,000 additional welfare benefit plans. Together, these plans hold about $15.2 trillion in assets.Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.Read the notice of proposed rulemaking on Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights.

entry.title: Agencies Announce Dollar Thresholds for Applicability of Truth in Lending and Consumer Leasing Rules for Consumer Credit and Lease Transactions
entry.content:
The Federal Reserve Board and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau today announced the dollar thresholds used to determine whether certain consumer credit and lease transactions in 2027 are subject to certain protections under Regulation Z (Truth in Lending) and Regulation M (Consumer Leasing).

By law, the agencies are required to adjust the thresholds annually based on the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, known as CPI-W. Transactions at or below the thresholds are subject to the protections of the regulations.

Specifically, based on the 3.9 percent annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, Regulation Z and Regulation M generally will apply to consumer credit transactions and consumer leases of $76,300 or less in 2027. However, private education loans and loans secured by real property, such as mortgages, are subject to Regulation Z regardless of the amount of the loan.
